provenance.source_path: internal derivation: WKF quote-process notes, NSN 4730-00-536-2210 (2026-01-08)
provenance.extraction_method: unzip -p on the docx for word/document.xml, then the w:t text nodes joined in document order and split on w:p paragraph boundaries. The extracted text is pure ASCII: zero em dashes, zero smart quotes, zero ellipsis glyphs.
provenance.cross_check_note: The docx itself was readable, so every string in this file is transcribed from the docx and the docx is the source of record. Handoff section 4.4a quotes the same document and was compared line by line as a check: every finding and every principle quoted in 4.4a is present in the docx with the same wording. The handoff was used only to confirm the transcription and to name the feature each consideration seeds. It was NOT used as a substitute source.
provenance.carries_no_arithmetic_note: Unlike the 1650-01-059-8221 pricing fixture, this document contains no computation to reproduce. Its acceptance test is about signal choice and disposition, never about arithmetic. The two fixture kinds do not substitute for each other.

expert_framing_quote: Thought process as I look for indicators on if we should quote it:
disposition_condition_quote: if you can buy The parts from adept fasteners at a great price
expert_bottom_line_quote: Bottom line if you can buy The parts from adept fasteners at a great price you can sell them to DLA added substantial margin because of the past purchase price.
elevation_basis: The elevated features are taken ONLY from the sentence the expert himself labelled Bottom line. That sentence names two things: buying from a named supplier at a great price, and the past purchase price. Nothing else is elevated.
ordering_note: The considerations appear in the order he wrote them. He states no ranking anywhere in the document. This fixture therefore infers no importance from position, and any code that treats list order as a ranking is reading something the source does not say.
